subject.title: fix: carry reply metadata into runtime context

question: May runtime-only turns elevate channel-supplied quoted reply text into the system-prompt path, or must reply body text remain untrusted while only an explicitly reviewed identifier subset is carried separately?
rationale: This is a durable model-trust contract across channels and context engines; a mechanical patch cannot safely choose which externally sourced reply fields are trusted.

options.title: Keep reply bodies untrusted
options.body: Route quoted/body text through the existing untrusted hidden runtime context and reserve any system-level data for a narrowly defined reviewed identifier contract.

options.title: Adopt trusted runtime reply context
options.body: Explicitly document and approve a channel-normalization trust contract that permits reply text in system context, with cross-channel security validation.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Defer the runtime-only handoff until the broader reply-context contract has an owner-approved trust model.

recommendation.title: Keep reply bodies untrusted
recommendation.body: Route quoted/body text through the existing untrusted hidden runtime context and reserve any system-level data for a narrowly defined reviewed identifier contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the current prompt/runtime-context split that this PR extends.
